guide.verdict: Custom OAuth 2.0 app for customers' Box (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)).

composio.note: Composio lists a managed Box toolkit; Box MCP is a separate bring-your-own-app toolkit. Create the auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio's managed app works. For launch you likely want your own app for branding, scopes and dedicated quota. Box also requires each customer's admin to authorize an app by its Client ID.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand, not Composio's
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across Composio users
Custom scopes, including scopes available on request
Own rate limits and shorter polling intervals

prerequisites.title: Developer Console access
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account or an enterprise account gives access to the Developer Console. MFA is needed to view the client secret.

prerequisites.title: Paid enterprise account for extra scopes
prerequisites.detail: Free trial accounts cannot request extra scopes. Some scopes also need add-ons such as Governance.

steps.title: Create the app in Developer Console
steps.detail: Choose User (OAuth 2.0) or Server type. The type cannot be changed later.
steps.done_when: App exists with the right type

steps.title: Draft scope list and justifications
steps.detail: Pick minimum scopes and write justifications; the developer must justify scopes to customer admins.
steps.done_when: Scope list and justifications are ready

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect URI
steps.detail: Set scopes and add the Composio redirect URI under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI. It must match exactly.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret from the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Send Client ID to customer admin
steps.detail: The admin adds the app by Client ID in Admin Console, Platform Apps. Enterprise developers submit for approval from the Configuration or Enablement tab.

steps.title: Wait for admin approval
steps.detail: The admin approves and the developer gets an email. Reports show a week or more.

steps.title: Request extra scopes by support ticket
steps.detail: Submit a ticket from a paid enterprise account explaining why the scope is needed.

traps.title: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000
traps.detail: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.

traps.title: Server apps fail until authorized
traps.detail: Calls with a service account token return unauthorized_client until the enterprise authorizes the app.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: Enterprise developers must resubmit to their Box Admin after changing scopes.

traps.title: Refresh tokens are single-use and expire
traps.detail: A refresh token lasts 60 days and works once. Store the newest one, or users must re-authorize.

traps.title: Developer token is for development only
traps.detail: It is an ordinary 60-minute access token tied to the signed-in console user.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: Box rejects mismatches, and duplicate URIs cannot be saved.

traps.title: App type cannot be converted
traps.detail: Switching between User and Server requires a new app.

blockers.symptom: unauthorized_client: This app is not authorized by the enterprise
blockers.what_it_means: The Server app has not been authorized by a Box Admin.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the enterprise admin to authorize the app by Client ID in the Admin Console.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin request with the Client ID and scope justifications.

blockers.symptom: Approval stays pending for a week or more
blockers.what_it_means: The customer's admin has not approved it; Box cannot speed that up.
blockers.what_to_do: Chase the customer's admin. Box says to file a support ticket after one week.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft follow-up messages to the admin.

blockers.symptom: Admin asks why scopes are needed
blockers.what_it_means: The developer must justify requested scopes to the admin.
blockers.what_to_do: Send a short written justification per scope.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: * **Scope should contain the minimum set of permissions required to perform the corresponding action:** So even if some end-user of your application uses the token directly against the API, they can't gain access beyond what you intended them to provide through the UI Element.

evidence.question: G4

This scope should always be included in the Token Exchange request.
evidence.answer: Every UI Element has a base scope with the least permissions needed for it to function, and the base scope must always be included in the token exchange request.
